duplicate_crc.note: byte-identical (md5 a008d9e8929c47c1a87edebebd2318ad). CPropertyManager::Register lets the LAST scanned file win; because the two files are identical the collision is harmless, but CRC -> file is not a 1:1 mapping.

summary.schema_conformance: 2113/2113 files parse. ZERO schema violations: no missing required key, no unexpected key, no extension/PropertyType mismatch, no key out of std::map order, no malformed body line, no non-canonical CRC text.
summary.shadowflag: present on ALL 1734 Buildings (1706 = '1', 28 = '0'), never on any other type. It is nominally optional but is universal in shipped data - emit it on every new Building.
summary.corpus_crc_resolution: 1684 distinct CRCs are referenced by the 142-map corpus; 1684/1684 (100%) resolve against this catalog. Zero dangling references.
summary.tree_constants: treesize is 1000.000000 on ALL 85 Trees and treevariance is 0.000000 on ALL 85. Neither key carries information in shipped data - they are required-but-constant. Emit exactly those two literals on any new Tree.
summary.shadowflag_semantics: The 28 shadowflag=0 Buildings are all thin or alpha-cut geometry that a blob shadow would smear: 10 chain props (5st_chain_001..008, flame_chain_001..008), 3 fences (5st_fence_002..004), 3 rock_pillar, ice_pillar_s05, icicle_up_05, cliff_wall_up, 3 treasure_hunt_rock, treasure_hunt_cave_01, boss_d_gate_01, ep-007-itemshop. 20 of the 28 also have NO .mdatr, i.e. they are decorative and non-colliding. Rule of thumb: shadowflag=0 iff the mesh is thin/see-through.

isattributedata.confined_to: b/ exclusively - 152 of 152. Zero occurrences across the other 40 top-level folders.
isattributedata.verdict: A GENERATION MARKER, not a semantic flag. It is emitted only by the original Empire-B authoring pass and by no later tool run. It is inert at runtime.
evidence: Value is '0' on all 152 files, single-valued - it carries no information by itself.
Perfectly confined to b/: 152/152 IA files sit under b/, while 207 of b/'s 359 Buildings lack it.

The b/10.gongyong (common) B_general_obj_NN family cuts exactly at a generation boundary: _01 through _17 all carry it (17/17); _18 through _42 and every later clone (_01_1.._01_4, _05_1, _10_1, _21_1, _25_1, _25-2) all lack it (0/32). Same shape in b/02: 'ob-11-01-skeletontower' carries it, 'ob-11-01-skeletontower01'..'06' do not.
It does NOT mean 'has collision data': .mdatr exists for 144/152 IA files and for 203/207 non-IA b/ Buildings - statistically identical - and 8 IA files have no .mdatr at all.
It does NOT track shadowflag: all 152 IA files are shadowflag=1, but so are 1554 of the 1582 non-IA Buildings.
It does NOT track corpus usage: 141/152 IA and 174/207 non-IA b/ props are placed somewhere.

No reader exists: grep for 'isattributedata' across WorldEditorRemix Srcs/**/*.cpp,*.h,*.py returns zero hits. EterLib/AttributeData.cpp (CAttributeData) is the .mdatr loader and never consults a property key.
isattributedata.generator_guidance: Never invent it. Preserve it verbatim when round-tripping an existing b/ property or the file stops being byte-identical. Never add it to a new property.

reserve.role: The retired-CRC tombstone list. WorldEditor appends a property's CRC here when the property is deleted, so that CRC is never reissued to a new asset. Legacy maps may still hold areadata.txt records pointing at a retired CRC; CPropertyManager::Get finds nothing and CArea::__Load_LoadObject silently drops the record - a retired CRC degrades to an invisible object, never a crash. Reissuing one would resurrect the wrong model in every legacy map that still references it.
reserve.verified: All 16 are disjoint from the 2112 live CRCs (set intersection empty), and none of the 16 appears in any of the 48774 areadata.txt records across <CORPUS>. The retirements are clean - no map still points at a tombstone.
reserve.write_trap: The shipped file terminates every record with \r\r\n, not \r\n - a text-mode append onto a string that already ended in \r. The engine tokenizer splits that into two breaks, so every CRC is followed by a blank line. Blank lines are skipped so it is harmless, but reproduce it byte-for-byte on rewrite.

identity_traps.filename_is_not_the_property_name: Some .prb files are named <model>.gr2.prb (e.g. b/10.gongyong/hay_01.gr2.prb, guild_construction/forge.gr2.prb, n/milgyo/milgyo_pavilion.gr2.prb) - the '.gr2' is part of the stem, not a second extension, and in those files PropertyName often keeps the '.GR2' too. Never derive a name or a CRC from the filename; read line 0 and the propertyname key.

building_gr2.b1-NNN-<role>: Empire-B city buildings, a hard 3-digit serial plus an English role word (b1-006-castle, b1-007-itemshop, b1-009-hotel, b1-010-bank, b1-011-workhouse). This is the most readable naming Ymir ever used.
building_gr2.ob-<biome>-<NN>[-<role>]: 'ob' = object. The FIRST number is the b/ sub-biome index, matching the numbered Korean folder: ob-7-* lives in b/03.ungwichon, ob-10-*/ob-11-* in b/02.gamyeom&haegoltap (infection & skeleton tower), ob-12-* in b/05.mudeumga (graveyard), ob-4-*/ob-5-* in b/07.milgyosawon (esoteric temple). The biome number in the NAME is the reliable one; the folder number is a later re-filing.
building_gr2.general_obj_<thing>: the shared clutter vocabulary - bottle, brazier, brimstone, campfire, carriage, drum, fence01..03, flag, jar_{blue,red,yellow}0N, lamp, pieceofstone0N, pillar, stump, txtstone, woodchair. English, singular, descriptive. Read these directly.
building_gr2.B_general_obj_NN / obj-NNNN / ob-N-NN: OPAQUE SERIALS. 246 Buildings (14% of all Buildings) carry a pure catalogue number with no descriptive token at all. You CANNOT tell what these are from the name - you must open the .gr2. This is the single biggest gap in name-based reasoning about the vocabulary.
building_gr2.<prefix>_ mirrors the zone: ep_ = eastplain, wdc_ = whitedragoncave, gls_ = geuglagsa, dmw_ = dawnmistwood, smh_ = Demon Tower, nsm_ = n snow map, 5st_/4st_ = temple stage N, 12t_ = 12-zodiac temple, sn_ = snow, mt_th_ = Mt Thunder. A prefixed clone (ep_B_general_obj_36) is a re-skinned copy of the b/ original for that zone.
building_gr2.size/shape suffixes: _01.._NN = variant; _1.._4 appended to an already-numbered name = a later clone of that exact variant; -corner / -lin / -lin2 / -door = wall tile roles (corner piece, straight run, straight run alt, doorway); _up / _low = vertical half; _s0N = small.

dungeonblock_gr2.note: DungeonBlocks are room-sized tiles snapped together to build an interior. The name is the ROOM ROLE, and it is consistently English: startroom, bossroom, eggroom, passage0N, passis / passic (passage-straight / passage-corner), three-way, conerroom, stonecave, dungeon_bN, stair. 361 of the 195 DungeonBlock model paths sit under d:/ymir work/zone/dungeon/<dungeon-name>/.
